On Contiki,SpecAgentverifies 137 out of 163 targets, again exceeding Preguss (133) and SpecSyn (92). On the more challenging Atomthreads project,SpecAgentsuccessfully verifies 109 of 239 targets, slightly below Preguss (112) but above SpecSyn (85), AutoSpec (99), and Codex (101). As described in Section 4.3, the programs were originally intended to evaluate Preguss, an approach focusing on excluding potential RTEs. The relatively stable performance of Preguss across these programs suggests its effectiveness on verification targets concerning RTE-freeness. Codex provides a relatively competitive baseline, but its performance remains belowSpecAgentand Preguss, indicating that a general-purpose agent alone may not consistently produce specifications sufficient for verification. It is worth noting that SpecGen verifies none of the targets on X509 and only a small fraction on Contiki and Atomthreads.

SV-COMP.The programs retrieved from the SV-COMP benchmark are mainly toy examples (average LoC being 27.79), on which the verification tasks primarily focus on the synthesis of loop invariants. Among 269 targets,SpecAgentsuccessfully verifies 218, substantially outperforming SpecSyn (132), Preguss (139), and AutoSpec (165), while remaining competitive with Codex (206), indicating thatSpecAgentpossesses a strong capability to reason about iterative program behavior and synthesize inductive invariants that capture non-trivial loop semantics. In contrast, Preguss and SpecSyn, which perform relatively competitively on some real-world repositories, show substantially lower coverage on SV-COMP, suggesting that their strengths on real-world RTE-oriented properties may not transfer equally well to loop-invariant synthesis. Codex, in contrast, achieves 206 successful verifications and remains close toSpecAgent, indicating that its general-purpose code reasoning capability is particularly effective on the relatively small SV-COMP programs.

text: 6.1 Cost Analysis. We further analyze the computational and monetary overhead of the evaluated approaches in terms of wall-clock time, Frama-C invocations, LLM calls, and API cost. As shown in Table 5,SpecAgent requires 1,684.49 seconds and 25.58 Frama-C calls per program, far more efficient than verificationintensive approaches (Preguss and SpecSyn). Although the wall-time overhead over lightweight approaches (AutoSpec and SpecGen) is non-negligible, it remains substantially lower than the human effort required for real-world verification projects (e.g., developing ACSL specifications and completing the verification of X509-parser required five calendar months of manual effort [16]). Moreover,SpecAgentrequires 99.40 LLM calls, slightly fewer than Preguss (107.30), with monetary cost being $0.6228, lower than Preguss ($0.7210) and Codex ($0.7100) while comparable to SpecSyn ($0.6243). Among the baselines, AutoSpec achieves the lowest overhead across all metrics. text: Internal Threats.First, LLM-based agents may produce different outputs across runs due to the stochastic nature of generation, introducing potential variance into specification qualities. We mitigate this threat by fixing the model configurations across experiments and reporting aggregate results over a series of evaluated tasks. Second, our ablation study incrementally adds major components to the basic candidate-generation workflow, but adding a component may also change the subsequent execution trajectory and the number of agent interactions, making it difficult to completely isolate its individual contribution. We therefore interpret the ablation results as measuring the contribution of each component within the overall workflow rather than as strictly independent causal effects. Finally, the effectiveness ofSpecAgentmay be sensitive to agent budget configurations, e.g., the maximum number of agent invocations.

text: Finally, the effectiveness ofSpecAgentmay be sensitive to agent budget configurations, e.g., the maximum number of agent invocations. Concerning this threat, our additional study on specification quality evolution shows that specification quality improves noticeably within the first 6–8 agent invocations, after which it tends to plateau, indicating that insufficient budgets can noticeably degrade specification quality, while larger budgets yield diminishing returns. The analysis provides empirical insights into the sensitivity ofSpecAgentto agent budget and how to configure the budget in practical scenarios. External Threats.The main external threat lies in the benchmark adopted for experiments. Although the benchmark programs come from real-world open-source repositories, the number of programs in the adopted benchmark is still limited. We mitigate this threat by evaluating the baselines across multiple repositories and complementing the experiments with real-world verification tasks. Further evaluation on larger and more diverse software systems is left for future work.

title: SpecAgent: Empowering Program Verification with Agentic Synthesis of Formal Program Specifications
text: Further evaluation on larger and more diverse software systems is left for future work. Another threat concerns the language scope, as our evaluation focuses on C programs specified in ACSL and verified with the Frama-C/WP ecosystem. The effectiveness of the proposed agentic workflow may depend on the characteristics of this programming language and formal verification ecosystem, and therefore our findings may not directly generalize to other specification languages and programming languages. Lastly, our evaluation relies on Frama-C/WP to assess specification correctness and strength. The verification tool is inherently incomplete, and a valid specification may fail to be proved due to limitations of the underlying solver, leading to potential false negatives in our evaluation. Nevertheless, we employ the same Frama-C/WP version, verification configuration, and underlying solver environment across all experiments and baselines, ensuring the consistency and fairness of the comparisons. , Vol. 1, No. 1, Article .

text: LLM-based Agent for Software Engineering.Recent advances in LLMs have shifted software engineering automation from mere LLM queries toward autonomous agents that iteratively interact with software environments. Early efforts such as MetaGPT [26] and ChatDev [44] focus on code generation by organizing software development as collaboration among role-specialized agents through predefined workflows for design, coding, and testing. As agentic capabilities evolve, recent works extend to repository-level tasks involving existing software. SWE-agent [ 57] addresses real-world GitHub issues by enabling agents to navigate repositories, edit files, and execute tests through a specialized interface. AutoCodeRover [60] incorporates program structures and iterative code search for issue localization and program repair. RepairAgent [9] enables autonomous defect repair by allowing LLMs to gather information, generate patches, invoke validation tools, and adapt actions based on feedback. OpenHands [52] further explores general-purpose software engineering agents that interact with code, command-line tools, and development environments. Despite this progress, agentic approaches for formal methods remain relatively nascent. Tu et al.

title: SpecAgent: Empowering Program Verification with Agentic Synthesis of Formal Program Specifications
text: Tu et al. [51] introduce AutoRocq, an LLM agent that performs program verification in the Rocq prover by iteratively refining proofs based on prover feedback. Sun et al. [50] employ LLM agents to orchestrate model checking tasks by selecting strategies, analyzing counterexamples, and refining decisions based on checker feedback. Compared to these works,SpecAgenttreats formal specification synthesis as the primary task, perform agentic generation, repair, and refinement on formal specifications. LLM-based Program Specification Synthesis.The emergence of LLMs has enabled specification synthesis beyond conventional rule-based and analysis-based approaches. AutoSpec [54] pioneers LLM-based specification generation by leveraging static analysis to expose program hierarchies and guide synthesis. SpecGen [33] combines conversational generation with heuristic mutation operators to repair generated specifications, while Preguss [53] employs abstract interpretation to detect potential runtime errors and guide generation. SpecSyn [34] further utilizes non-equivalent program mutations to assess and refine the semantic strength of generated specifications. Pei et al. [42] and Cao et al.

title: SpecAgent: Empowering Program Verification with Agentic Synthesis of Formal Program Specifications
text: [42] and Cao et al. [11] improve specification generation by fine-tuning LLMs on specificationrelated corpora. Compared to these works,SpecAgentreformulates specification synthesis as an agentic decision-making process, where specialized agents dynamically determine generation, repair, and refinement actions based on evolving context. Other works [12, 28, 56, 61] target different specification languages, such as Verus for Rust. Due to substantial differences in programming languages and formal verification ecosystems, we do not directly compareSpecAgentwith these approaches. Among them, StarVerus [28], a concurrent work, explores autonomous agents for synthesizing and repairing formal specifications using verifier feedback. However, its primary objective is to obtain specifications that pass verification, without explicitly critiquing their strength. In contrast,SpecAgenttreats specification correctness as a prerequisite rather than the endpoint, explicitly identifying semantic deficiencies in the specifications and refining them when necessary.

title: SpecAgent: Empowering Program Verification with Agentic Synthesis of Formal Program Specifications
text: We presentSpecAgent, an agentic framework for automated ACSL specification synthesis that reformulates specification generation as an iterative decision-making process. By integrating planning, generation, verification-guided repair, and critique-guided refinement,SpecAgentidentifies and revisits specification dependencies rather than following a fixed forward-only workflow. Extensive evaluation on real-world specification generation and verification tasks demonstrates thatSpecAgentimproves specification completeness while maintaining high precision, effectively supporting practical software verification. These results highlight the potential of agentic approaches for reliable and scalable formal specification synthesis. , Vol. 1, No. 1, Article . Publication date: October 2026.
